title: New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, Completions — November 2026 data) — the other leaf of GDPNow's residential node, six days past the funding cliff
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes), row "New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, and Housing Completions) | December 17, 2026 | 8:30 AM | November 2026", release code A202612170830, reference A202611. Corroborated by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet, whose 2026-12-17 08:30 row reads "Housing starts, Import and export prices". Filed `estimate` per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an in-sweep discovery, and doubly so because the same Census page demonstrably carries `Suspended` rows. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). Why it earns its own row: GDPNow's residential-investment node has two leaves and this corridor was tracking neither. The model workbook's Residential sheet (GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx, fetched direct 2026-09-06) routes `valExHomeSales` into `FRSBKX_USNAqtr` ("Brokerage commissions") and `SplicedNewHousingConstruction` into `FRSPX_USNAqtr` ("Permanent-site" construction) — so the 12-09 EHS print moves the commissions leaf and this print moves the construction leaf, which is the far larger of the two. The measured signature of the commissions leaf is small (140 EHS vintages move the residential contribution a median 0.0376pp against 0.0057pp baseline, p<0.0001); nothing in this session measured the construction leaf, and the initial research should. Second reason, and the sharper one: this is a CENSUS release, so unlike its 12-09 and 12-17 NAR neighbours it sits SIX DAYS PAST the 2026-12-11 expiry of PL 119-103. It lands 08:30, ninety minutes before NAR's Pending Home Sales Index the same morning (proposed separately) — two residential prints on one date with opposite funding exposure, which makes 12-17 the corridor's cleanest read on whether the cliff bites. Sibling ledgers have arrived three times independently at "Census cancels previews and keeps reports" (intl-trade-full-report-2026-12-08, advance-economic-indicators-2026-12-28, wholesale-trade-2026-12-09); this print is a fourth test of that rule on a series none of them measured. Impact LOW and symbols empty: no house playbook is macro- or housing-keyed, and the homebuilder ETFs were measured inert on the neighbouring EHS release days (ITB 1.911% vs a 1.839% baseline over 122 sessions since 2016, p=0.40) — whether they are inert on a STARTS/PERMITS print is an open question this lane did not test and the initial research should. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
